exposure: Perinatal asphyxia (induced by umbilical cord clamping)
outcome: Cardiovascular hemodynamics (arterial blood pressure, regional blood flow, carotid blood flow (CBF), mean arterial pressure (MAP))
Need for chest compressions for return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC)
Time for MAP to return to baseline after ROSC
cohort: The study included preterm growth-restricted lambs and control lambs, where FGR was induced in one twin at 89 days gestation, and experiments were performed at 126 days gestation.
finding: Preterm growth-restricted lambs demonstrated resilience during mild perinatal asphyxia, evidenced by prolonged CBF maintenance and reduced need for chest compressions, but exhibited CBF overshoot after ROSC which may increase the risk of cerebrovascular injury.
